title: personal console triage playbook - ryan
content:
Quick note: this is my personal triage scratchpad for console/observability work. Not formal runbook yet — just a brain dump so I don't forget small checks and follow-ups.

Date: 2026-03-13

Morning priorities
- check INF-9876 (customer reported slow dashboard loads)
- follow up with infra on noisy indexer alerts (OBS-1042)
- triage any new high-sev errors in console-prod for last 6h

Inbox / triage queue (fast pass)
1) INF-9876: "dashboard load times > 10s for EU customers"
   - first-pass: look at frontend traces (zipkin) for requested dashboard: "Dashboard: tenant-views-over-time"
   - quick query: BigQuery logs (console-prod.logs) filter by request.path = "/console/dash" AND geo.region = "EU" AND timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 6 HOUR)
   - early finding: increased tail latency correlated with repeated 503s from routing-service (see trace ids attached to ticket)
   - tmp mitigations: disable heavy widget (top_tokens_heatmap) via query param "lite=true" recommended to customer, open feature-flag to gate heatmap in EU region
   - follow-ups: assign to Leo for routing-service trace investigation, ask infra to check NLB target health in eu-west-1

2) OBS-1042: indexer noise -> spikes in indexer_cpu and disk-io alarms at 03:20-03:45 UTC
   - logs: loki query: {job="indexer"} |= "OOM" or |= "killed" | json | count_over_time({job="indexer"}[1m])
   - quick note: correlates with nightly batch job "kv-cache-refresh" (scheduled 03:15) — possible contention with snapshot job
   - mitigation: throttle kv-cache-refresh (reduce concurrency from 16 -> 6) and re-run in canary cluster
   - action: Priya to submit infra-change request, mark as scheduled change, watch for regressions next nightly window

Open bugs / oddities seen while hunting
- metric gaps on "token-cost-by-route" around 02:50 UTC — sometimes missing 1-2m windows; hypothesis: exporter outage / prometheus relabeling race. ACTION: check prometheus operator logs and remote-write retry counts.
- alert flapping: "console-high-error-rate" firing ~3x in last 24h; seems triggered when we have slow requests + retry storm. Need to add smarter dedupe in alert policy (sustained 5m vs instantaneous).

Reproduction steps (for customer INF-9876)
1. Use curl with header X-Region: EU and Authorization token for affected org
2. Hit /console/dash?name=tenant-views-over-time with query param preview=false (to mimic heavy load)
3. Capture server timing and X-Trace-Id headers; push traces to zipkin / trace UI
4. If reproduces, capture p95/p99 and attach to ticket; if not, try with account-specific filters (some orgs have huge embedding counts which triggers heavy aggregation)

Debug checklist (personal)
- [ ] Confirm route-level fallback behavior for routing-service (does fallback add extra latency?)
- [ ] Check whether KV cache misses spike during reported window (grafana: kv-cache/miss-rate)
- [ ] Validate streaming vs non-streaming codepath timeouts (codepath-switch flag?)
- [ ] Attach pcap/ELB logs if NLB suspected

Notes to file with infra
- If NLB unhealthy targets found: ask infra to rotate targets and enable cross-zone load balancing for eu-west-1 test pool. Mention impact on 503s seen in traces.
- Consider temporary capacity bump for routing-service under dedicated pools to reduce queuing until kernel-level fixes are deployed.

Escalation criteria (quick)
- If > 100 EU tenants report dashboard slowness within 1h -> escalate to on-call infra and paging list
- If error rate > 5% sustained for 10m on console-prod -> open SEV / notify pm and cs leads

Quick queries to run (copy/paste)
- BigQuery: SELECT service, COUNT(1) as errors FROM `console-prod.logs` WHERE severity >= "ERROR" AND TIMESTAMP >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 6 HOUR) GROUP BY service ORDER BY errors DESC LIMIT 50;
- Loki: {job="frontend"} |= "504" | json | count_over_time({job="frontend"}[5m])
- Prometheus: rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="console"}[5m]) by (le, route)

Meeting notes / syncs
- 10:30 sync with Leo (routing-service debug). Goals: identify whether code path or infra (NLB) is root cause; decide on canary config to reduce concurrency.
- 15:00 quick triage with CS (INF-9876 customer) to share temporary workaround and expected timeline for fix.

Thoughts / long-term ideas
- Add per-region widget-level throttles so heavy visualizations can be automatically degraded in high-latency regions without global impact.
- Improve observability of query complexity from UI widgets (expose estimated-rows / cost metric for dashboards so we can auto-suggest "lite" mode).

Unresolved questions
- Why did token-cost-by-route metrics drop for 1-2m? exporter or prom relabel race? need to reproduce locally with remote-write failover test.
- Is there a correlation between nightly kv-cache-refresh and indexer CPU spikes on other clusters?

Follow-ups (assigned)
- Leo: routing trace deep-dive (due EOD) - add root-cause hypothesis to INF-9876
- Priya: infra change request to throttle kv-cache-refresh (due tomorrow morning)
- Asha: draft customer note for INF-9876 with temporary workaround (due before 15:00 sync)

End of scratchpad.

Random quick thought: if we add a lightweight "preview" flag to dashboards and make it default for first load, we might cut median render time in half for heavy tenants. Worth prototyping behind a feature flag.

-- ryan
